subject: Life Skills
title: In-Group and Out-Group Bias
description: A quick win: understand In-Group and Out-Group Bias.

hook.text: Split kids into two random teams at camp. Within hours, each team believes the other cheats, lies, and is inferior.

buildup.text: Henri Tajfel's minimal group experiments showed that even meaningless labels — 'Group A' vs. 'Group B' — create bias.

discovery.text: Your brain gives in-group members more trust, empathy, and benefit of the doubt. Outsiders get suspicion by default.

twist.text: The bias is not hate. It is a shortcut. Your brain uses group labels to simplify a complex social world.

climax.text: Expand your in-group deliberately. Shared goals, shared meals, shared stories — exposure dissolves the boundary.

punchline.text: We vs. them is the oldest trick. Build a bigger we.

quiz.question: What did Tajfel's experiments prove about in-group bias?
options: It only forms between genuinely different groups
Even meaningless, random group labels create bias
It is a conscious choice people make deliberately
